```
  def allowedInstrumentsBasedOnCorporateProfile(
    customerId: UUID,
    maybeTradingAccountType: Option[TradingAccountType],
    maybeGoalType: Option[InvestmentGoalType],
    instruments: Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto],
    maybeInvestorTypes: Option[Set[InvestorType]],
    maybeFromInstrumentIds: Option[Set[String]],
    maybeLocale: Option[Locale]
  ): Future[AllowedInstrumentsResponse] = {
    corporateCustomerJdbcRepository
      .findById(customerId)
      .flatMap {
        case Some(corporateCustomer) =>
          corporateProfileJdbcRepository.findById(corporateCustomer.corporateProfileId).flatMap {
            case Some(corporateProfileData) =>
              innerAllowedInstrumentsBasedOnCorporateProfile(
                Some(corporateProfileData),
                maybeTradingAccountType,
                maybeGoalType,
                instruments,
                maybeFromInstrumentIds,
                instrumentCache,
                ProductLine.FundSmartProductLine,
                maybeLocale
              ).map {
                case (resolvedInstruments, exclusiveInstruments) =>
                  createAllowedInstrumentsResponse(resolvedInstruments, exclusiveInstruments, maybeTradingAccountType, maybeInvestorTypes)
              }
            case None =>
              throw new Exception(s"Unable to find the corporate profile [${corporateCustomer.corporateProfileId}]")
          }

        case None =>
          Future.successful(
            createAllowedInstrumentsResponse(
              resolvedInstruments = filterBaseInstruments(instruments, maybeFromInstrumentIds),
              exclusiveInstruments = Map.empty,
              maybeTradingAccountType = maybeTradingAccountType,
              maybeInvestorTypes = maybeInvestorTypes
            )
          )
      }
      .withRetry(AlwaysRetryOnException)
      .recover {
        case ex =>
          logger.error(
            s"deriveAvailableInstrumentIdsBasedOnCorporateProfile failed for customer $customerId, " +
              s"tradingAccountType $maybeTradingAccountType, goalType $maybeGoalType",
            ex
          )
          AllowedInstrumentsResponse(List.empty, Map.empty)
      }
  }

  def allowedInstrumentsBasedOnCorporateProfileForTenant(
    tenantId: UUID,
    maybeTradingAccountType: Option[TradingAccountType],
    maybeGoalType: Option[InvestmentGoalType],
    instruments: Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto],
    maybeInvestorTypes: Option[Set[InvestorType]],
    maybeFromInstrumentIds: Option[Set[String]],
    maybeLocale: Option[Locale]
  ): Future[AllowedInstrumentsResponse] = {

        }
      }
      .withRetry(AlwaysRetryOnException)
      .recover {
        case ex =>
          logger.error(
            s"deriveAvailableInstrumentIdsBasedOnCorporateProfile failed for Tenant $tenantId, " +
              s"tradingAccountType $maybeTradingAccountType, goalType $maybeGoalType",

          )
          AllowedInstrumentsResponse(List.empty, Map.empty)
      }
  }

  def allowedInstrumentsBasedOnCorporateProfileForGroup(
    groupId: String,
    maybeTradingAccountType: Option[TradingAccountType],
    maybeGoalType: Option[InvestmentGoalType],
    instruments: Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto],
    maybeInvestorTypes: Option[Set[InvestorType]],

  ): Future[AllowedInstrumentsResponse] = {
    corporateProfileJdbcRepository
      .findById(CorporateProfileEntity.groupProfileId(groupId))
      .flatMap { corporateProfileData =>
        innerAllowedInstrumentsBasedOnCorporateProfile(
          corporateProfileData,
          maybeTradingAccountType,
          maybeGoalType,
          instruments,
          maybeFromInstrumentIds,
          instrumentCache,
          ProductLine.FAManagedBespokeProductLine,
          maybeLocale
        ).map {
          case (resolvedInstruments, exclusiveInstruments) =>
            createAllowedInstrumentsResponse(resolvedInstruments, exclusiveInstruments, maybeTradingAccountType, maybeInvestorTypes)
        }
      }
      .withRetry(AlwaysRetryOnException)
      .recover {
        case ex =>
          logger.error(
            s"deriveAvailableInstrumentIdsBasedOnCorporateProfile failed for Group $groupId, " +
              s"tradingAccountType $maybeTradingAccountType, goalType $maybeGoalType",
            ex
          )
          AllowedInstrumentsResponse(List.empty, Map.empty)
      }
  }

  private def innerAllowedInstrumentsBasedOnCorporateProfile(
    corporateProfile: Option[CorporateProfileData],
    maybeTradingAccountType: Option[TradingAccountType],
    maybeGoalType: Option[InvestmentGoalType],
    instruments: Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto],
    maybeFromInstrumentIds: Option[Set[String]],
    instrumentCache: LocaleAwareInstrumentCache,
    productLine: ProductLine,
    maybeLocale: Option[Locale]
  ): Future[(Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto], Map[String, Set[InvestmentGoalType]])] = {
    val baseInstruments = filterBaseInstruments(instruments, maybeFromInstrumentIds)

    val rules = corporateProfile.flatMap(profile => profile.configuredRules.get(productLine)).getOrElse(List(UnRestricted))
    val baseInstrumentIds = baseInstruments.map(_.id).toList
    val eligibleInstrumentsResponse = corporateProductRuleInterpreter.calculateEligibleInstrumentIds(
      maybeTradingAccountType = maybeTradingAccountType,
      maybeGoalType = maybeGoalType,
      rules = rules,
      availableInstrumentIds = baseInstrumentIds
    )
    val allEligibleInstrumentIds = eligibleInstrumentsResponse.eligibleInstruments
    val eligibleInstrumentIds = maybeFromInstrumentIds
      .map(allEligibleInstrumentIds.intersect)
      .getOrElse(allEligibleInstrumentIds)
    val added = eligibleInstrumentIds -- baseInstrumentIds
    val locale = maybeLocale.getOrElse(Locale.defaultLocaleByRegion(region))
    for {
      newInstruments <- instrumentCache.getCachedInstruments(instrumentIds = added, locale = locale, withMstarDocs = false).map(_.values)
      finalList = baseInstruments.filter(i => eligibleInstrumentIds.contains(i.id)) ++ newInstruments
    } yield (finalList, eligibleInstrumentsResponse.exclusiveInstruments)
  }

  private def filterBaseInstruments(
    instruments: Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto],
    maybeFromInstrumentIds: Option[Set[String]],
  ): Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto] = {
    maybeFromInstrumentIds
      .map(fromInstrumentIds => instruments.filter(x => fromInstrumentIds.contains(x.id)))
      .getOrElse(instruments)

patterns.title: Flatten positive charge fees then fold by FeeRateType and TradingAccountType

context.operation: [INV-5456] feat(charge, communication): Fee charge estimate email to include EAM fee
context.trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

patterns.concern: Large interim nested map only regrouped later; zero ignored and negative not expected
patterns.requested_change:
So this `groupedEstimatesWithFeeRateType` is not used anywhere, other than to be grouped again… i.e. there’s no value to create this interim map

And it’s quite big map in fact, `Map[FeeRateType, Map[TradingAccountType, List[PlanFeeQueryResult]]`

‌

Can you consider sth like this?

* flatten the fee breakdown, and filter for positive value upfront - we don’t entertain zero, and we don’t expect negative entries
* then we fold into expected shape `Map[FeeRateType, Map[TradingAccountType, BigDecimal]]`

```scala
estimatedFeesByFeeRateType = estimateResponse.planFees
  .flatMap(
    pf =>
      pf.feeBreakdown
        .getOrElse(List.empty)
        .filter(_.accumulatedChargeableFee > 0)
        .map(c => (c.feeRateType, pf.tradingAccountType) -> c.accumulatedChargeableFee)
  )
  .foldLeft(Map.empty[FeeRateType, Map[TradingAccountType, BigDecimal]]) {
    case (accByFeeRateType, ((feeRateType, tradingAccountType), fee)) =>
      accByFeeRateType.updatedWith(feeRateType) {
        case Some(innerAccByTradingAccountType) =>
          Some(innerAccByTradingAccountType.updatedWith(tradingAccountType) {
            case Some(accumulatedFee) => Some(accumulatedFee + fee)
            case None                 => Some(fee)
          })
        case None =>
          Some(Map(tradingAccountType -> fee))
      }
  }
```

patterns.requested_change:
Yea the aggregate logic will follow MStar always, as long as it returns something. We only retain existing MStar doc if somehow MStar doesn’t return for that docType\+locale group.

The risk of what you said is there, but:

* We already retry \(I’ll change to retry for both exception type, only skip if sth else unexpected\)
* Most of the time, the 2 sources match. Only for some rare cases, they have disparity
* And the thing is, sometimes indeed MStar remove newest docs. It could be their mistake but it’s easier for us to follow them and raise to MStar to correct their data, instead of us trying to maintain something we don’t own \(I think\)

‌

Ideally, I would want to capture the fact that sth fails and we fallback as well, i.e.

* if both sources succeed, we merge and trust MStar 100%
* if one fails, we fallback to empty and still use the other successful one, but we won’t trust 100% and maybe log error to check

But the problem is same as what I explained in the exception retry comment, for no docs response, MStar sometimes gives valid xml with empty node, but it also sometimes give empty payload \(causing parsing exception\). And worst is it’s not consistent, empty payload can be retried and can give valid xml later. So we can’t be for sure.

‌

I think for first cut, let’s go with this and we monitor more across the daily runs to see if we can improve further.

patterns.requested_change:
Maybe something like this

```
case class EventTagRecordInput(...other fields...)

case class EventTagRecord(
  ordering: Long,
  ...other fields...
)

object EventTagRecord {
  def fromInput(input: EventTagRecordInput, ordering: Long): EventTagRecord = ...
}
```

‌

Table with proper required auto-incrementing PK

```
class EventTagTable {

  def ordering: Rep[Long] = column[Long]("ordering", O.PrimaryKey, O.AutoInc)
  ...other columns...

  override def * : ProvenShape[EventTagRecord] =
    (ordering, persistenceId, eventManifest, event, tag, addedAt).<>((EventTagRecord.apply _).tupled, EventTagRecord.unapply)

  def projectionForInsert =
    (persistenceId, eventManifest, event, tag, addedAt).<>((EventTagRecordInput.apply _).tupled, EventTagRecordInput.unapply)
}
```

‌

```
trait EventTagDao {
  def insert(item: EventTagRecordInput): Future[Long]
  def readNext(n: Long)(tag: String, from: Long): Future[List[EventTagRecord]]
}
```

‌

```
class EventTagDaoJdbc extends EventTagDao {
  def insert(item: EventTagRecordInput): Future[Long] = {
    val insertQuery = table
      .map(_.projectionForInsert)
      .returning(table.map(_.ordering))
      .into(EventTagRecord.fromInput)

    db.run(insertQuery += item).map(_.ordering)
  }
}
```

‌

Then in every usage of EventTagRecord, we have proper required `ordering` field instead of having to check optional.

* We are using the same event with latest timestamp here. That means a few months from now, if someone looks at the customer entity inspect, it would be pretty tough to know if this was a re-answer by customer, or it was a system patch.

patterns.requested_change:
Just to summarize a bit so that we’re on the same page.

‌

We have 2 levels of logic to determine if a fund is a standalone fund:

* derived logic based on fund attributes \(i.e. semi-liquid, redemption regulations, lots size, non-daily schedule\)… these are “rules” to auto qualify funds as standalone, without Ops having to configure anything
* a “forced” flag to explicitly set a fund as standalone, even if they don’t check any of the above boxes… e.g. large NAV funds

  
On `InstrumentInfoDto` \(static configuration of instrument data\), as of current PR, FE will only see the forced flag, but not the derived one. Hence on advisory instrument-list / instrument-details endpoints, BE would resolve both of the above and send a single resolved flag to FE to tell if a fund is effectively a standalone or not. This way FE can implement UX logic to guide customer for fund selection, so all that is good.

‌

If customer lands on a deeplink with TAA to portfolio summary screen \(i.e. bypassing FE guardrails on fund selection\), we need to tell FE if such TAA is valid or not:

* if we handle everything properly, we would need to return it as warning/block flags at instrument level, so that FE can display properly \(similar to HK\)
* but since we agreed to descope this piece \(i.e. no FE display\), we want to ensure at least such request is blocked as early as possible, not allowing customer to continue all the way to OTP and then get 5xx error

This eager block can be a simple flag in portfolio summary response, and FE can handle \(error or proper failure popup with explanation\). Or we can go with generic BadRequest as well. This is up to yall to discuss.

‌

Another approach is to serialize the resolved isStandaloneFund flag in `InstrumentInfoDto` as a derived field as well \(i.e. not part of constructors, no setter, but part of json\). Then we leave it completely to FE to check the individual instruments' flag and handle.
constraints: Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.
Derived semi-liquid, redemption regulation, lot size, nondaily schedule; early flag/BadRequest or JSON-only derived InstrumentInfoDto field proposed; OTP-late 5xx unacceptable.

If customer lands on a deeplink with TAA to portfolio summary screen \(i.e. bypassing FE guardrails on fund selection\), we need to tell FE if such TAA is valid or not:

* if we handle everything properly, we would need to return it as warning/block flags at instrument level, so that FE can display properly \(similar to HK\)
* but since we agreed to descope this piece \(i.e. no FE display\), we want to ensure at least such request is blocked as early as possible, not allowing customer to continue all the way to OTP and then get 5xx error

This eager block can be a simple flag in portfolio summary response, and FE can handle \(error or proper failure popup with explanation\). Or we can go with generic BadRequest as well. This is up to yall to discuss.

‌

Another approach is to serialize the resolved isStandaloneFund flag in `InstrumentInfoDto` as a derived field as well \(i.e. not part of constructors, no setter, but part of json\). Then we leave it completely to FE to check the individual instruments' flag and handle.

Ideally this should contain sourcePlanId as well

I know we key by scheduleId, and itself will be sufficiently unique. Just thinking when we have the audit readside for these ack events, if anyone looks at the scheduleId alone, they will immediately want to know about sourcePlanId \(targetPlanId is already the current plan\). And here’s the “problem”, existing readside in goal/trading svc is latest snapshot only, even in entity we also don’t keep old schedules. Once a schedule is removed, it gets tricky to lookup their info again.

This is why I keep asking to at least include sourcePlanId in all these contexts.

patterns.concern: If rechecking, pass TransferRequest acks via InvestmentTransferProjection; if prior validation authoritative, identify investmentTransferRequestId and skip SIP only
patterns.requested_change:
If we want to perform the compliance check again \(potentially to block investment if SIP status changes in between the sell and buy leg\), we have to persist the acks in trading svc `TransferRequest` and pass it down when we call investment svc in `InvestmentTransferProjection#handleRedemptionCompletedEvt`.

If we accept that we have already validated before we trigger the redemption, and we can ignore if anything changes in between the 2 legs, we will need to skip the checks in investOnce call. The skip must be specific to SIP only, and we should continue to perform existing checks we do today. We can identify these investment request by checking existence of `investmentTransferRequestId`

patterns.title: Compare per-version timestamp PK with per-entity TTL upsert

context.operation: Initial EC POC Idea
context.trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

patterns.requested_change:
Let’s consider 2 approaches:

1. Each row is one version

    * pk `((entity_type, entity_id), timestamp)`
    * ttl for each row
    * insert only
    * every version will create tombstone via ttl
    * allow us to query by timestamp
    
2. Each row is one entity

    * pk `((entity_type, entity_id))`
    * ttl for each row
    * cassandra insert is upsert by pk \(citation needed\), but def dont want to use update \(which requires read before write\)
    * every version will create tombstone via insert immediately, and via ttl for last version
    * cannot query by timestamp
    

‌

Last time we decide to store version in pk, was in context of pg which doesn’t support TTL, hence we needed the timestamp.

But with cassandra impl, we don’t need this anymore.
constraints: Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.

* flags to display warnings/blocks:

* actual data for impacted plans:

    * tell explicit if the details of the plans that are blocked or needs more ack
    

‌

So the endpoint you defined here matches the 1st one but DTO matches the 2nd one.

patterns.requested_change:
The idea \(at least for HK\) is we want single endpoint for flags so that FE can straight away know if a goal can have new investment or not, and if not, what the restrictions/warnings are. This should cater for all possible blockage reasons.

OTOH, in specific pages \(e.g. Risk Profile / PI / DPM\), we only want to tell the plans that are affected by those data in isolation.

That’s why we split the endpoints this way so that FE can just call exactly what they need. We can bring this up again to discuss with FE friends, but keep in mind that we will need to add more types of warnings/blocks soon \(e.g. no-longer-AI-customers still holding AI-only funds, TAA containing buy blocked instruments, recurring schedule with missing CKA exemption acks, CPF/SRS account closure, etc.\)

patterns.requested_change:
I think we discuss that instrument specific constraint is not well understood yet, and we should keep it out of entity.

The “alts” bit is business use case, the logic doesn’t care if it’s alts or not, we simply match instrumentId \(against TAA vs AAA, single-fund vs multi-fund portfolio?\).

Even if at the point of voucher creation / constraint update, we verify the specified instrumentId is indeed alts at that point in time \(I don’t see the validation in this PR\), how should it behave if the instrument is no longer alts \(we do have some instruments current tagged as alts but IO/CX wants to change to liquid alts in future\)? Alts or not is an attribute of goal’s productline. Today it’s also most 1:1 due to alts instruments are forced to be single fund portfolio, but we don’t know the future state.

This is why if we want to do instrument specific voucher, we should just keep it that way. Alts logic, if any, should just be at logic layer.

Inside we call lockOnce which will throw if unable to lock. We might change to some other flavour of locking method to enable retry etc, but eventually it will still throw. This will propagate the exception to the caller. If caller is akka projection / kafka subscriber, we would then restart the event by tag query / consumer subscription.

patterns.concern: Starved A heartbeat lets B revoke/acquire; A completion must not delete B lock; Futures not cancelled
patterns.requested_change:
Since we can’t cancel future, in some extreme scenario \(thread starvation \+ too aggressive `unlockDelay`\) \(or at least in theory\), we might run into a race condition such that:

* task A acquires the lock and goes on with its long running logic
* thread starvation / CPU constraints causes the heartbeat ack to miss updates
* aggressive `unlockDelay` enables other tasks to be able to take over the lock
* task B revokes the lock of task A - this never cancels the currently running task A
* task A finally completes, now attempts to release its lock

Here we call delete instead of deleteRequest, that means task A would remove the task B’s lock

‌

patterns.requested_change:
Fee range must be configured for all trading accounts at the point of firm onboarding. Missing config for CPF/SRS should be treated as data/setup issue, and we must not use it as FE feature toggle.

* Linking/displaying account should be supported regardless of existence of fee range config
* Add goal flow can be changed to fail instead of fallback to empty fee range, so that FA can escalate

‌

Moreover, current impl is too fragile:

* Data is returned in full shape. Should a customer be able to view such config of the firm, even if they belongs to same firm?
* No RBAC / No ownership guards: once authenticated, anyone can call the endpoint by providing a customerId. Think customer/fa of Firm X calling the endpoint with customerId of Firm Y

‌

We shouldn’t need this endpoint for this purpose of show/hide CPF/SRS features in FE \(at least not driven by missing data\).

If any, this endpoint is only useful when we want to display/manage firm’s fee range config in Advisor Portal, by PartnerOps or some super-FAM \(as opposed to manually controlled by Endowus Ops\)

When such requirement comes, we would still need proper RBAC resource for this tenant level data \+ new CanActionForTenantGuard

CC

patterns.title: Remove live full-redemption recheck from invalid-order replay handling

patterns.concern: Cmd already established no full redemption; later live request must not suppress processing or alerts and leave trade stuck
patterns.requested_change:
If we want additional check, then we need to think about our future reader:

* One who follows the code would see that the cmdHandler already checks for ongoing full redemption, and that if `INVALID_ORDERS_GENERATED_BY_FEE_CHARGE` is thrown, that cmdHandler already validates there is no ongoing full redemption trade in the PlanTraderEntity
* Now in projection, we again query again, but this time we check on redemption svc. This query is also live at the point of projection processing the event \(which can be replayed\), so it’s very possible that at this point, there is full redemption returned here
* Then this code simply goes to do nothing and return

‌

There would be 2 wrong things in such scenarios:

* The live full redemption request \(from redemption svc\) at this point should not have any effect on this processing logic
* This fee redemption trade would be stuck due to invalid orders, and we do not have any alerts at all

‌

I’d suggest to remove this check, unless we know there’s some corner cases that might happen

‌

```scala
  protected def customTradingAccountTypeOrdering: Ordering[TradingAccountType]

    instrument.tradingConfigDetails.allowedInvestorTypes
      .filterNot(blacklistedInvestorTypes)
      .flatMap { investorType =>
        investorTypeCcyToTradingAccountMapByRegion(region)
          .get((investorType, instrument.ccy))
          .onNone(logger.error(s"No matching trading account for $investorType for instrument ${instrument.id} of ccy ${instrument.ccy}"))
      }
      .toList
      .sorted(customTradingAccountTypeOrdering)

```

I’m a bit confused about the sequence. If I understand correctly:

* existing schedules do not have `nextUpcomingDate`, and the processor would send `TriggerRecurringInvestmentTransferCmd` for all entities \(customer \+ trading account\)
* current impl in this PR would:

    * if not meant to be triggered yet, only emit `NextUpcomingInterGoalTransferDateUpdatedEvt`
    * if meant to be trigger, only emit `RecurringInvestmentTransferRequestedEvt` or `UpcomingInvestmentTransferScheduleDetectedEvt`, but `nextUpcomingDate` is not updated
    
* in the projection, if `RecurringInvestmentTransferRequestedEvt` but failed validation, then trigger `UpdateNextUpcomingInterGoalTransferDateCmd`

‌

patterns.concern: Never means subscriber started or failed-to-start
patterns.requested_change:
`RestartSource.onFailuresWithBackoff` sets `maxRestarts = Int.MaxValue`, i.e. this future shouldn’t complete with a failure

```
* Wrap the given [[Source]] with a [[Source]] that will restart it when it fails using an exponential backoff.
*
* This [[Source]] will never emit a failure, since the failure of the wrapped [[Source]] is always handled by
* restarting. The wrapped [[Source]] can be cancelled by cancelling this [[Source]].
* When that happens, the wrapped [[Source]], if currently running will be cancelled, and it will not be restarted.
* This can be triggered simply by the downstream cancelling, or externally by introducing a [[KillSwitch]] right
* after this [[Source]] in the graph.
*
* This uses the same exponential backoff algorithm as [[akka.pattern.Backoff]].
```

‌

But ok if we don’t trust akka, then these 2 log entries are a bit misleading

* On Success, it means that the kafka subscription has been gracefully stopped. This is either during graceful shutdown, or something really went wrong \(cuz we don’t really stop our kafka consumer for normal topic - only the TaskTopicSubscriber supports this\). Nevertheless, it surely doesn’t mean “the subscriber has started”
* On Failure, then something unexpected went wrong with the `RestartSource`. But it also doesn’t mean “the subscriber failed to start”, it just means the subscription stream was terminated with \(potentially fatal\) error

patterns.title: Do not replay new goal projection into same live plan table

context.operation: Feature/DATA-1522 new column to support product line with type view
context.trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

patterns.requested_change:
It will definitely cost a bit to start a new projection, but otherwise load itself on Cassandra or PG should be ok.

Having said that, we need to be careful with this GoalJdbcProjection. It’s writing to both goal & plan readside tables, with some handlers take data from event while some other handlers fetch latest data from entity.

Here we only wish to upversion goal table, but not plan table. Running this V5 projection as is will cause a long window of inconsistent data in plan table, for extended period of time until the projection has caught up to latest offset.

We can consider a few options:

1. Upversion both goal & plan tables, even if no changes to plan table’s schema
2. Upversion only goal, and perform double release to switch over:

    1. Release 1:
    
        1. projectionV4 writes to goalV4 \+ planV4
        2. projectionV5 writes to goalV5
        
    2. Release 2 \(after projectionV5 has caught up\):
    
        1. projectionV4 writes to goalV4
        2. projectionV5 writes to goalV5 \+ planV4
        3. Ideally we switch when lag is zero, but even if there’s any, the window of inconsistent data is much smaller
        
    
3. Since new column is derived data \+ optional in schema, and we only care about latest value, we can consider using alter table add column approach. And add a sync endpoint \+ kafka tasks to populate it for all goals \(with some basic optimistic locking check\)

‌

\(1\) is most straightforward but cost us the most. \(3\) requires somewhat more development effort, but will cost us the least. \(2\) is somewhat middle approach, tradeoff some PG writes \(still same cost of Cassandra reads\) with release logistics.

patterns.requested_change:
Idempotent means if same request is called twice \(or more\), we are able to de-dupe and execute it only once. Full fledge solution would involve properly implement `IdempotencyKey` , but for now, it should be sufficient if we rely on existing mechanism in `investment` svc to allow caller to set `investmentRequestId` via `requestIdSeed`

When a task is fully approved, workflow-engine will trigger this endpoint to perform the request \(sent in task payload\). The guarantee here is at-least-once. So we have to make sure we don’t invest multiple times if for whatever reason, it’s triggered multiple times by workflow-engine.

patterns.requested_change:
Since we don’t need `FilterOrder` in instrument side. I think it’s cleaner to move it to advisory `FundSmartFilter`, and make it region specific.

They are almost the same between SG and HK, but it’s ok to keep them separate:

* it’s the same rationale that we have region specific `getAllEligibleDisplayTags`
* it’s clearer to define which sections are applicable for each region, rather than define a common set and each region take out a few not-applicable ones, e.g. in this case, if I’m writing for `SgFundSmartFilter`, I have no idea about `CiesSectionName` at all, but I still have to remember to remove it from the list

‌

I guess either approach is fine, but I think let’s try to be consistent \(since we already spend the effort refactoring this\).

Whether we make it common in InstrumentTags OR region specific in FundSmartFilter, let’s use sae approach for both filters and displayTags. Currently we use common for filters, but region specific for displayTags

patterns.requested_change:
I was testing this PR in dynamic ,and new nodes with this change simply couldn’t join the existing cluster. Even complete scale down to 0 and 3, and the new nodes couldn’t form a cluster together. It only “see” itself.

Spent so much checking the release notes to find any incompatibility issue, only to realize much later that we have this manual join step when defining the Lagom ServiceClient

* it’s not even required to use the ServiceClient since this is purely http via the service locator

I can’t recall why we added this initially, but I think it makes sense to remove it

patterns.requested_change:
Testing completed. The change helps to reduce the AskTimeout occurrences during pod restart/deployment, however do not remove it completely.

‌

Test setup: a simple client that repeatedly hit an endpoint that would hit an entity & interfere with the cluster while the client is running and observe any errors

```
execFut {
  Source
    .tick(1.second, 100.millis, "tick")
    .runForeach { _ =>
      if (counter.incrementAndGet() % 100 == 0) {
        logger.info("Still running")
      }
      Source(1 to 10)
        .map(_ => UUID.randomUUID())
        .mapAsync(4) {
          chargeService.getPlanProfile(_).invoke().recover {
            case e => logger.error(s"FAILED with ${e.getMessage}")
          }
        }
        .runWith(Sink.ignore)
    }
}
```

‌

Before the change:

* Delete any node \(simulate node consolidation\) would trigger the AskTimeout errors, particularly worse if the node is currently the ShardCoordinator \(oldest node\)
* Rolling restart \(i.e. simulate deployment\) would trigger AskTimeout errors

‌

After the change:

* Deleting non-ShardCoordinator node does not trigger any AskTimeout errors. No errors from the ShardCoordinator either
* Deleting ShardCoordinator node still trigger a few AskTimeout errors, however much fewer number of errors as compared to before the change. Still no errors logged by the new ShardCoordinator, so it’s likely just extra latency caused by the shard rebalancing. Indeed can observe less AskTimeout errors if deleting the node when the shard allocation is more even. Could be related to [
[…incidental material or intervening source omitted…]
* Rolling restart exhibit similar pattern: no errors for younger nodes, fewer errors for the oldest ShardCoordinator node

‌

I can try with the experiment to enable faster shard rebalance in next PR \([
[…incidental material or intervening source omitted…]
introduced since v.2.6.10 with a note that it would be the new default however disabled by default, and only rebalance one shard at a time\), but I think this one is good to go.

patterns.concern: Empty default instructions cannot distinguish never-initialized from upserted-then-deleted plan state.
patterns.requested_change:
The entity state is default with empty fee instructions, it means the plan always exists, just without any data. Modelling it this way means you can’t distinguish between a uninitialized plan vs a plan with upserted-then-deleted fee instructions.

If we care enough about this, then we probably should make state a sealed trait, default with case object NotInitialized, otherwise it’s case class Initialized\(feeInstructions\). Then you can throw for GetCmd/DeleteCmd on NotInitialized. And no-op without error if deleting already deleted fee instruction for Initialized, and even throw if deleting last entry for Initialized \(to ensure there’s always an entry to support the fee rate query\)
constraints: The sealed NotInitialized/Initialized state is conditional on caring about that distinction; no-op deletion and last-entry rejection are proposals within that model.

patterns.concern: effectiveEndDate is derived, cannot be reconstructed at event-creation state by projection, and changing one instruction generally affects two instruction end dates.
patterns.requested_change:
Just thinking out loud, I’m not sure about capturing this effectiveEndDate in the event

* It’s derived data, but I understand the concern that projection is not able to derive by itself since projection does not have access to the state at the point of event creation
* It’s somewhat incomplete, because we would typically affect effectiveEndDate of 2 instructions, but we only emit for the one being upserted / deleted

If the intention is to provide ability for projection \(or even external topic subscriber\) to reconstruct the exact state, we can consider emit 2 events instead, one for the individual change, and one for the state \(pattern “Event-Carried State Transfer”\). This comes with its own pros & cons, but I think it’s cleaner and more flexible than stamping single effective end date here.

patterns.title: Review: I think we should:
patterns.context: PR 10262 (Feat/INV-3637 bff endpoint upload document), no inline path; original row 434.
patterns.concern: Document upload has no customer context, whereas GET must verify customer/context ownership in the domain edge service.
patterns.requested_change:
I think we should:

* create new endpoint in document svc `/api/v1/document/upload` with this UploadDocumentRequest type \(maybe optional documentId if there is need to control this id from caller\), and its logic calls `createDocumentWithBinaries` providing the OTHERS value for the deprecated enums
* create authenticated endpoint in BFF proxy to above endpoint in document svc, for advisor portal, ~~which requires \(CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT resource & Create permission\)~~
* do not allow for client portal for now, since there is no planned flow that requires this yet

‌

Later on when we add GET endpoints, then it will be applicable for both advisor portal and client portal, ~~both require \(CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT resource & Read permission\)~~

Unlike the POST upload endpoint which doesn’t care about the context of document, the GET ones must care and validate the document indeed belongs to the customer \+ context. Hence these GET endpoints will have to be edge in the context service, e.g. goal/customer svc instead of direct document svc. This means these services would be responsible to capture the generated documentId from the upload endpoint.

‌

Example for add goal flow:

* FA uploads document in advisor-portal → calls BFF to proxy to document svc → advisor-portal captures generated documentId
* FA confirms to create the add-goal approval request in advisor-portal → calls BFF to proxy to advisory svc, which eventually creates workflow in workflow-engine

    * The workflow request must contain all the documentIds associated with this add-goal request
    
* When workflow request is fully approved → workflow-engine calls advisory svc which calls goal svc to create goal

    * We need to somehow persist these documentIds to the goalId
    
* When customer retrieves suitability doc from goal page in client-portal → calls BFF to proxy to goal svc `GET /api/v1/goal/:goalId/document` or `GET /api/v1/goal/:goalId/document/:documentId`

    * BFF validates goalId belongs to customerId
    * goal svc validates documentId belongs to goalId
    

‌

patterns.title: BffServiceImpl: In on-behalf operations:
patterns.context: PR 10258 ([INV-3639] feat(bff): Capture and propagate Customer/Employee context in BFF), bff-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/bff/impl/BffServiceImpl.scala; original row 469.
patterns.concern:
In on-behalf operations:

* auth user would be employee, which we would set into context using EmployeeProvider
* and the request \(either payload or query param\) should specify the customer, which we would use to validate proper ownership/relationship in guards

‌

Once it reaches the handler \(logic layer\), it is up to the domain to decide how they want to implement it. Example:

1. they could use an endpoint in BE that expects customerId in either payload or query param \(and hence we can simply reuse it completely, and define it as proxy endpoint in BFF\)
2. they could set context using CustomerProvider, and call the endpoint in BE that expects customerId from context instead \(and if not available, 500 error is rightfully thrown\)

I would prefer \(1\) instead and we stick to setting TenantId/CustomerId/EmployeeId context by auth only.

I think until then, let’s just leave it.

‌

patterns.title: PortfolioMonthlyChangesHelper: I think there are 2 types of race conditions we might see here:
patterns.context: PR 9603 (Feat/INV-3271 marketdata portfolio entity phase 1), marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/helpers/PortfolioMonthlyChangesHelper.scala; original row 718.
patterns.concern:
I think there are 2 types of race conditions we might see here:

1. We get event that instrument mc is updated, and we trigger this method which will query instrument mc from readside - that might not have latest data yet… cuz they are 2 independent projections

    * We override the data for the instrument being updated, but it’s not bullet proof, e.g. db projection is super lagged for some reason
    
        * event of instrumentA, its data A2 is overridden on top of existing readside A1 & B1
        * then event of instrumentB, its data B2 is overridden on top of stale A1 & B1
        
    
2. Multiple instruments might be updated at once, each of them triggering this method… their upsert might override each other

    * This was protected with Portfolio entity last time. So we might need some impl of optimistic locking here
    

‌

patterns.title: SgRecommendedInvestmentManager: Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls
patterns.context: PR 9739 (Feat/EN-3683 sg create a new api to get recommended investment amount), advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/managers/sg/SgRecommendedInvestmentManager.scala; original row 783.
patterns.concern:
Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls

```
lazy val tierLevelFut = getCustomerIncomeTierLevel(customerId)
lazy val myInfoFinancialDataFut = getMyInfoFinancialData(customerId)

tradingAccountType match {
  case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_SGD_CASH_ACCOUNT =>
    tierLevelFut.map { level =>
      deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountSgdCashBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
    }

  case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_CPF_OA_ACCOUNT =>
    for {
      myInfoFinancialData <- myInfoFinancialDataFut
      response <- deriveRecommendationFromMyInfo(myInfoFinancialData) match {
        case Some(recommendation) =>
          Future.successful(recommendation)
        case None =>
          tierLevelFut.map { level =>
            deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountCpfBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
          }
      }
    } yield response

  case _ =>
    Future.successful(RecommendedInvestmentDto.noRecommendation())
}
```

‌

No need to split the helper methods too fine, especially when they are not used in more than one place

* `getCustomerIncomeTierLevel` can do both customer lookup and perform mapping to TierLevel
* `getMyInfoFinancialData` can do myinfo lookup, if found then return, else only then do onboarding lookup and perform mapping

‌

patterns.title: ReportApplication: Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.
patterns.context: PR 9306 (Feat/EN-3405 use tasktopicsubscriber in report for manual start/stop), report-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/report/impl/ReportApplication.scala; original row 1081.
patterns.concern:
Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.

In case of report, the svc itself is responsible for triggering of the topic producer side. So we can potentially just call start \(via distributed pubsub\) in the same trigger endpoint, i.e. `createMonthlyStatementsV2` first will trigger start, only then produce the message.

* the start is idempotent so if already started, it won’t cause any harm
* the distributed pubsub is at-most once tho, so it could still happen that maybe one of instance does not start… but I suppose this could be checked easily via logs or metrics.

‌

We can also make this pause/resume status persisted, and check upon startup :thumbsup: 

‌

patterns.title: Review: Trading team will:
patterns.context: PR 9296 ([INV-3070] revert(advisory): revert fx supported ccy validation in advisory endpoint), no inline path; original row 1083.
patterns.concern:
Trading team will:

* add supported ccy validation for indicative quote
* after cash reservation is accepted, this is validated again before we make the actual fx conversion - if error, will block the trade. TradeOps then can intervene as usual, i.e. delete/cancel the trade

‌

The above scenario can happen even if we add this validation in advisory. Example: ccy X is supported on T, we allow goal creation…. T\+1 something is wrong, and we remove support for that ccy… T\+2 investment is funded, and fxconversion will now fail

patterns.requested_change:

‌

Redemption: `TRADE_SUBMITTED_EXTERNALLY_PENDING_SETTLEMENT`

Charge: `WITHDRAWAL_IN_PROGRESS`

‌

Transaction: `SUBMITTED_EXTERNALLY_AND_PENDING_SETTLEMENT`

‌

Redemption: `DELETED` with `deletedAt`

patterns.title: TransactionTypes: We can let the old `FxConversionDetails` having optional accounts, as we are migrating away from this v1 model.
patterns.context: PR 8011 (TT-3566 Make broker account optional for FX transactions), transaction-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/transaction/impl/common/TransactionTypes.scala; original row 1585.
patterns.concern:
We can let the old `FxConversionDetails` having optional accounts, as we are migrating away from this v1 model.

For new `FxTransaction` model:

* Changing `debitBrokerAccount` and `creditBrokerAccount` to optional here makes sense. All existing fx conversion txn would have them populated, and hence still compatible with old FE.
* But I think it’s also good to capture the fact that broker accounts will be available when the txn is settled. Maybe we can consider the following:

    * Add new `SettledFxStatusDetailsV2` that is identical with `SettledFxStatusDetails` with additionally the 2 required broker account fields
    * Change kafka subscriber to populate transaction using V2 instead of V1
    * Add 2 required broker account fields into `SettledFxStatusDetailsDto`
    
        * If entity has V2, map as is
        * If entity has V1, require the outer optional broker account fields in `FxTransaction` to be defined
        
    

‌

patterns.title: RebateDistributionCommunicationsManager: Each customer wouldn’t have too many trailer rebates per quarter, so I suppose it’s ok to run this aggregation in memory. But we potenti...
patterns.context: PR 8353 (Feat/INV-1996/automate trailer rebate), rebate-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebate/impl/logic/managers/RebateDistributionCommunicationsManager.scala; original row 1620.
patterns.concern:
Each customer wouldn’t have too many trailer rebates per quarter, so I suppose it’s ok to run this aggregation in memory. But we potentially can push this down to database query and it would be more memory efficient \+ faster computation there.

Example in BQ. Then we can enrich the instrument \+ mandatory rebate data bits on the fly

```
SELECT
  r.customerId,
  r.broker,
  SUM(r.distributedRebateAmount),
  ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT r.instrumentId)
FROM
  silver_raw_dataset.rebate_distribution_requests r
WHERE
  r.fromDate >= '2023-07-01'
  AND r.toDate <= '2023-09-30'
GROUP BY
  r.customerId,
  r.broker
ORDER BY
  r.customerId,
  r.broker
```

‌

patterns.context: PR 7899 (PLATFORM-1097: Rebalance service pg readside migration), rebalance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebalance/impl/db/AuroraJdbcSchema.scala; original row 1715.
patterns.concern:
Ah yes, creating them as empty is ok. My previous comment was in context of either the repository or the dbHandler having injected database.

‌

Good examples:

```
_ <- database.run(someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithoutInjectedDatabase.createTable)
_ <- database.run(SomeDbHandlerOrRepositoryCompanionObject.createTable)
```

In these cases, the Schema class with its injected database will decide where to create these tables. Hence we will create them in correct place \(even tho non-read-side ones will be empty cuz we haven’t migrated\)

‌

Potentially confusing example \(previous version of this PR\):

```
_ <- someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithInjectedDatabase.createTable
```

Here, the injected database of Schema is ignored, and the dbHandler/repository will use its own injected database. And in this specific case, `rpcCommunicationDetailsJdbcRepository` and `planMarketValueJdbcHandler` both have only 1 instance using GCP jdbcDatabase.

‌

Either way, current PR looks good to me!

patterns.requested_change:
Even with separate processors, the chance of duplicated rows is still there because we perform 2 inserts for UpdatedEvt \(but yes, splitting the processors reduce this chance much further\)

Within the history processor itself, this can still happen for UpdatedEvt if:

* insert old succeeds, but insert new fails → retry for the event, which will insert old again

patterns.title: Post-Lagom API contract exception versus actor serializer; goal internal exception pattern unresolved
patterns.context: rebalance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebalance/impl/entities/rebalancer/handlers/TriggerThresholdBreachedRebalanceCmdHandler.scala; PR: [INV-1303] feat(rebalance): Increase min backoff to 1.5s
patterns.requested_change:
Yeah this is where the voodoo happens.



Before:

* SvcException extends Lagom TransportException which the Lagom ExceptionSerializer knows how to serdes them. The `LagomServiceExceptionHelper` is extra logic to help avoiding sentry spamming
* This same exception is also used to throw inside entity/cmdHandler. These can be serdes thanks to `JsonSerializer[AdvisorySvcException]`



After Lagom removal:

* SvcException in \*-api module are now intended as API contract only. They are converted to HTTP error via `EndpointResultCompat#mapToApiError`
* akka serdes now is configured as

```
akka {
  actor {
    serializers {
      play-json = "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializer"
    }
    serialization-bindings {
      "akka.Done" = akka-misc
      "akka.actor.Address" = akka-misc
      "akka.remote.UniqueAddress" = akka-misc
      "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializable" = play-json
    }
  }
}
```

* this is why if we want serdes to work… we need to extends `PlayJsonSerializable` \(all the state/cmd/evt do this\)
* however, it’s debate-able whether we want to add this to our API contract. You can see none of the services do this, except for goal svc



Goal svc does it in a subtle way:

* it creates another `GoalSvcException` inside goal-impl and throw this in entity/cmdHandler
* this is why serdes works for goal svc \(and only goal svc\)
* and if such internal GoalSvcException is propagate to http, it converts back to the goal-api GoalSvcException

```
  val ServiceErrorMap: Throwable => Throwable = {
    case logic.GoalSvcException(message, errorType) => GoalSvcException.toApiError(GoalSvcException(message, errorType))
    case e: GoalSvcException                        => GoalSvcException.toApiError(e)
    case e                                          => e
  }
```



So following goal svc should work - but I’m not sure if this is the right way to do it. Let’s think more before we mass apply this pattern

evidence.quote:
Yeah this is where the voodoo happens.

‌

Before:

* SvcException extends Lagom TransportException which the Lagom ExceptionSerializer knows how to serdes them. The `LagomServiceExceptionHelper` is extra logic to help avoiding sentry spamming
* This same exception is also used to throw inside entity/cmdHandler. These can be serdes thanks to `JsonSerializer[AdvisorySvcException]`

‌

After Lagom removal:

* SvcException in \*-api module are now intended as API contract only. They are converted to HTTP error via `EndpointResultCompat#mapToApiError`
* akka serdes now is configured as

```
akka {
  actor {
    serializers {
      play-json = "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializer"
    }
    serialization-bindings {
      "akka.Done" = akka-misc
      "akka.actor.Address" = akka-misc
      "akka.remote.UniqueAddress" = akka-misc
      "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializable" = play-json
    }
  }
}
```

* this is why if we want serdes to work… we need to extends `PlayJsonSerializable` \(all the state/cmd/evt do this\)
* however, it’s debate-able whether we want to add this to our API contract. You can see none of the services do this, except for goal svc

‌

Goal svc does it in a subtle way:

* it creates another `GoalSvcException` inside goal-impl and throw this in entity/cmdHandler
* this is why serdes works for goal svc \(and only goal svc\)
* and if such internal GoalSvcException is propagate to http, it converts back to the goal-api GoalSvcException

```
  val ServiceErrorMap: Throwable => Throwable = {
    case logic.GoalSvcException(message, errorType) => GoalSvcException.toApiError(GoalSvcException(message, errorType))
    case e: GoalSvcException                        => GoalSvcException.toApiError(e)
    case e                                          => e
  }
```

‌

So following goal svc should work - but I’m not sure if this is the right way to do it. Let’s think more before we mass apply this pattern

patterns.context: transaction-api/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/transaction/api/models/TransactionTypes.scala; PR: [INV-1437] feat(transaction): Models
patterns.requested_change:
My rationale on not-using-StatusFields for this is:

* StatusFields is a bridge to V1 to support these optional-per-status fields, e.g. requestedAmount is None and only populated when transaction is created, settledAmount is None and only populated when transaction is settled etc
* These fields are at top level in v1 TransactionDto, so the v2 to v1 mapping, we just blindly set them
* Whereas in this AssetTransfer case, the field is required in v1 \(since we create dedicated v1 DTO for it\), and the value is always populated either with requestedUnits or settledUnits. This means `statusFields.requestedUnits` wouldn’t be used anywhere, but when it’s used for AssetTransfer, we will call `Option.get`. This is why it looks off in my head.

1. The goal of this PR stays the same: build MV projection from timeseries `LatestPlanMarketValueUpdatedMsg` and any manual overridden via REST api

    1. In same subscriber, we should handle all `LatestPlanMarketValueUpdatedMsg`, do the timestamp checks and upsert all latest MV from timeseries
    2. We should use a new DTO, e.g. MarketValueProjectionData to capture not only the MV but also a flag indicating whether confirmedMV and assumedMV are in sync \(logic of `isValidLatestPlanMarketValueUpdatedMsg`, useful for migration logic later\)
    3. After upsert, retain the checks on `isValidLatestPlanMarketValueUpdatedMsg` and proceed if existing logic \(which we will migrate later\)
    4. We can use same subscriber \(same consumer group\) to help with migration later. If different consumer group, we would need to double-release, one to turn off the old subscriber with logic, follow ed by another release to include logic in new subscriber.

patterns.title: Kafka logger override in conf-reference, then Vault/config-map per-service level
patterns.context: report-impl/src/main/resources/logback.xml; PR: [EN-1248] chore(report): custom log config
patterns.requested_change:
If it’s urgent, I guess we can go ahead with this change for now. However, the better way I think is to change the logback.xml in conf-reference instead



You can make this override-able by:

```
<logger name="org.apache.kafka" level="${org.apache.kafka.log.level:-WARN}"/>
```



Then in the service you want to override, provide the custom log config as

```
<included>
  <property name="org.apache.kafka.log.level" value="INFO" />
</included>
```

  
This custom file will then be set in Vault in old SG setup, or mount via some config-map in the new kustomize setup

patterns.requested_change:
Since we do not have updates from `timeseries` yet, we can rely on rebalance updates itself. `timeseries` would already capture the pending order as soon as they are generated, however we only release when the buy trade is exported.

patterns.title: Independent dividend files: BadRequest nonretry and bounded TCP/unknown retry
patterns.context: dividend-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/dividend/impl/subscribers/HongKongEntitlementDividendTopicSubscriber.scala; PR: TT-1732 change dividendTopic to dividendFileTopic
patterns.concern: Since we can’t reliably reproduce and fix them, we want to limit the number of retries to avoid blocking the whole topic.
patterns.requested_change:
The ServiceLogic in dividend svc alreadymaps the scenarios it cannot handle the file to BadRequest. So we don’t want to waste time retrying for those case \(’s intention\).

There could potentially still be other exceptions that not caught by ServiceLogic itself, e.g. the case of big file and the tcp connection got cut during file processing. Since we can’t reliably reproduce and fix them, we want to limit the number of retries to avoid blocking the whole topic. patterns.requested_change:
So for acks, it’s somewhat tricky to correctly reverse it unless we inspect the old events. We might potentially return the old state as part of command, so one can use it as \(manual\) compensating saga. But then, we still need to carefully check before applying because of concurrent requests.

OTOH, most of the time it’s harmless to leave the ack there. We can build recon logic for ack too, e.g. CAT1 goals with persisted CAT2 ack, goals with recurring investment with persisted recurring ack. This way, we can eventually fix the acks without building complicated workflow logic. And it’s ok because this only affects recurring flow, unlike earmark which will affect CR calculation.

I can update the logging message here a bit to indicate that we will have recon for it, instead of just purely “can ignore”.

patterns.title: Pending order has amount or units; settlement both; mixed lists and latest-state model
patterns.context: transaction-api/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/transaction/api/models/TransactionTypes.scala; PR: INV-555 feat: Investment Transaction and Orders modelling
patterns.requested_change:
Do we have need to tell our consumer if order is unit or amount based? I think if that question ever comes up, it should be checked at source, rather than transaction.

So how about:

* pending order have amount and unit both optional, and a require clause to check at least one is populated
* assumed and confirmed order have amount and unit both required



A transaction can have mix of all of these in its order list. Then we don’t need to split too much:

* requested state
* pending state
* settlement state: either assumed or confirmed, once confirmed we don’t care about assumed data

patterns.requested_change:
FYI…

I and  chatted offline on this topic:

* The request provides the TAA together with corresponding acks for that specific TAA. We don’t need to look up again, even in rare race condition in which exists a TaaModificationEarmark for same plan. If such case happens:

    * goal modification request itself should already ack for its corresponding new TAA. So either one of the goal modification or investment request will have correct ack
    * investment orders will anyhow be generated much later by trading service - potentially using a different TAA at that time. As long as we guarantee all trading impact activities go thru latest ack check, it’s sufficient
    
* OTOH, CR calculation should lookup TAA honouring TaaModificationEarmark. This is because it can happen to another completely different plan, as CR breach is validation at customer level.



Conclusion, we don’t need to change anything here, except for maybe find a way to structure/comment code so that this logic is clear for reader. But we can revisit refactoring after we capture the essential logic \+ extensive test cases.

Memory usage wise it’s working well. It uses more memory, since we are aggregating plan’s MV in logic \(instead of DB\), but we can control how much by adjusting the mapAsync parallelism.

With parallelism = 4:

|  | **from\_date** | **Memory allocation rate** | **Time taken** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Aggregate in memory | 2021-10-01 | ~100MB/s | ~155s |
|  | 2021-01-01 | ~100MB/s | ~1,080s |
| Aggregate in DB | 2021-10-01 | ~10MB/s | ~2s |
|  | 2021-01-01 | ~10MB/s | ~15s |

‌

In terms of time, it’s clear that using DB aggregate functions is faster, but I’m not sure if it can cope when we have more plans \(hence the suggestion to in method 1 to find the planIds only\)

In staging, with from\_date = 2021-01-01

* query with SUM \+ MIN aggregate function would take ~15s
* query with DISTINCT plan would take ~6s, and afterwards, we would issue as many queries as plan count to get holdings per plan \(but these are all key fields, so should be fast\)

patterns.title: Message ordering needs the partition key and sequential processing within that partition
patterns.context: dividend-api/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/dividend/api/DividendService.scala; PR 3078: Fix/SILVER-11385 fix ordering msgs
patterns.requested_change:
Hmm I feel this comment is a bit misleading. Message ordering is only guarantee at partition level, that’s why we want to add partition key. Not because of how consumers consume the messages.  
  
If we don’t add partition key AND consumers consume with single thread, they will still run into out-of-order issue, because messages of same entity are spread to multiple partitions.

If we add partition key, BUT consumers still consume with multiple threads, they will still run into out-of-order issue, because of multiple threads in same partition.  
  
So we need to add partition key \+ consumers using parallelism = 1 if we really want to maintain the message ordering

patterns.title: JSch connected/isConnected flags and closed socket state are distinct checks
patterns.context: silver-commons/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/commons/sftp/PooledChannelFactory.scala; PR 3332: SILVER-12449: Report service improments
patterns.requested_change:
`Channel#connected` is the logical field when we call connect/disconnect on the Channel. `Channel#isConnected` also checks the `Session#isConnected` flag which again is another field driven by connect/disconnect method.

‌

`Channel#closed` is more about the underlying socket connection.

‌

Typically, these two should correspond with each other, i.e. not connected and closed, or connected and not closed. However, since nothing guarantees, we might as well check both. JSch itself checks both to determine if channel is broken or not.

patterns.requested_change:
Something to think about. This app server call to create PDF will actually do 2 things:

* create the PDF
* call document service to upload the file to GCP → this will trigger eventually trigger communication to send email

Existing code, right after this, will persist the documentId to report’s cassandra table - which will be used to determine if reprint is required later on.

If the pod crashes between these 2 steps, report generation is not idempotent, i.e. duplicate documents created / duplicate emails sent to user.

‌

With this change, we somewhat widen the gap with another step to upload to SFTP. Should we consider uploading to SFTP after we persist? If fail to upload, we can retry? Or the generate metadata file part can also attempt uploading if documentId is in csv data, but not found in SFTP? Or we simply log error, which raise sentry and we manually drop the file - should be infrequent enough?

‌

patterns.requested_change:

If we throw, the code path will involve the whole try catch, whereas if we use `Future.failed` it will just return the exception as it.

I guess for us, this doesn’t matter too much. Personally I just feel using `Future.failed` more naturally when we are already in a future scope. Both have same effect.

patterns.title: Final optional event fields defer optional-forever versus mandatory-plus-migration choice
patterns.context: dividend-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/dividend/impl/entities/dividend/ces/DividendEvents.scala; PR 2833: SILVER-11229: Fix settlement date for dividend reinvestment
patterns.requested_change:
All new fields are now optional in events, hence all JsonMigration steps are removed.

We can:

A. Keep them optional forever to correctly reflect the event history, i.e. they are indeed new fields that were added at some point of time.

B. Make them mandatory \+ add back the migration step to provide default value in separate release

‌

\(A\) would force new event processors to think and handle them, since all events will be re-processed by them. They might fallback to default values, or not. \(A\) give them an obligation to handle, but a choice to choose.

\(B\) effectively forces all new event processors to follow the default value via the serializer.

‌

Making them optional now defer the decision of choosing \(A\) or \(B\) of out scope of this PR.

patterns.title: FX daily-price conversion separates missing prior rate from mapping outcome and uses HALF_EVEN scale 2
patterns.context: marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/entities/instrument/processors/InstrumentMarketDataEventProcessorForMultiCcy.scala; PR 2600: removes failing when fx rate is not present for instrument price calculation in another ccy
patterns.requested_change:
Nit: This log doesn’t feel right, cuz now we club the case when fxRateToUse is None, and then case when `.map(fxRateToUse => { blah } `produces None. I know it’s not possible for that map to produce None, but still :stuck_out_tongue: 

‌

Maybe like this is better?

```
convertedDailyPrices = sortedDailyPrices.flatMap { dailyPrice =>
  fxRates
    .filterNot(_._1.isAfter(dailyPrice.priceDate))
    .sortBy(_._1.toEpochDay)
    .lastOption match {
      case None =>
        log.error(s"unable to find the fx rate [$instrumentCcy|$targetCcy] for the date [${dailyPrice.priceDate}], skipping for the date")
        None

      case Some(fxRateToUse) =>
        val convertedPrice = (dailyPrice.value * fxRateToUse._2).setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN)
        Some(DailyPrice(businessDate = dailyPrice.businessDate, priceDate = dailyPrice.priceDate, priceCcy = targetCcy, value = convertedPrice))
    }
}
```

‌
